pretreatment: Glass substrates (Carl Roth/Menzel) were cleaned in an ultrasonic bath with acetone, ethanol, and water.
surface_functionalization: Twenty micromolars of biotin-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) were diluted with a ratio of 1:10 in 2 /C2saline sodium citrate (2 /C2SSC) buffer and immobilized on the glass substrate as linker molecules. The linker molecules were exposed to UV light (254 nm) for 20 min. The glass slides were washed for 10 min with 0.1 /C2saline-sodium citrate/0.5 sodium dodecyl sulfate (0.1 /C2SSC/0.5%SDS) to remove any unbound molecules.
evidence: Glass substrates (Carl Roth/Menzel) were cleaned in an ultrasonic bath with acetone, ethanol, and water. Twenty micromolars of biotin-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) (Euro ﬁns MWG Operon, Ebersberg, Germany) were diluted with a ratio of 1:10 in 2 /C2saline sodium citrate (2 /C2SSC) buffer and immobilized on the glass substrate as linker molecules. To bind the ssDNA to the glass substrate, the linker molecules were exposed to UV light (254 nm) for 20 min. After this, the glass slides were washed for 10 min with 0.1 /C2saline-sodium citrate/0.5 sodium dodecyl sulfate (0.1 /C2SSC/0.5%SDS) to remove any unbound molecules.
